title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

reading.body:
This is a misuse failure rather than a malfunction. A license plate reader network performed the function it was built for, and the person querying it held the authority to do so. The failure sits at the point of access, where a legitimate credential was turned to a personal purpose, tracking two private individuals rather than supporting police work.

Because the operator was an authorised user, no model-level or data-level safeguard would have flagged the queries as wrong. Catching it would have required review of query logs against a stated investigative purpose, or a check that tied each lookup to a case. The system had no way to distinguish a lawful query from an unlawful one on its own.

What is not established is the exact scale of the conduct. The headline reports 164 uses and the summary reports 228, and the given facts do not reconcile the two figures. The account rests on a Kansas certification order and on reporting, and it is not established from these facts whether any criminal or civil proceeding followed.

reports.title: Kansas police chief used Flock license plate cameras 164 times to track ex-girlfriend

summary: In Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Lee Nygaard reportedly used Flock Safety license plate readers 228 times from June to October 2023 to check the whereabouts of his ex-girlfriend and her new boyfriend, according to a Kansas certification order. The order said he also followed them in a police vehicle and admitted that jealousy influenced his conduct. Nygaard resigned in October 2023 and later lost his police certification.
